newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says France soon able to import gene-maize.
newsitem.headline: EU says France soon able to import gene-maize.

text.p: France will shortly be able to import genetically-modified maize after receiving official notification of a decision to allow its sale in Europe, a Commission spokesman said on Thursday.
The European Commission on December 18 cleared imports of maize developed by Swiss firm Ciba Geigy AG and grown in the United States.
"Notification is imminent," the spokesman said, adding that this would mean that imports could then go ahead.
"Anything else would be rather odd as they were the ones who asked for it (clearance of genetically modified maize.)"
But France has said it would approve the sale and production of genetically-modified maize only when new EU labelling rules, promised by Environment Commissioner Ritt Bjerregaard, have been adopted.
The spokesman said that this would take some time.
France has warned that it will draft its own labelling rules if the EU does not move fast enough.
French customs officials customs officers in the port of Saint-Nazaire this week seized a second cargo of U.S. by-products believed to contain genetically-modified maize.
Environmental groups, including Greenpeace, and consumer groups have demonstrated against imports of genetically-modified farm products saying they may endanger human health.
